32.0.0.en: 1 And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, in the first day of the month, that the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, take up a lamentation for Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say unto him, Thou art like a young lion of the nations, and thou art as a crocodile in the seas: and thou camest forth with thy rivers, and troubledst the waters with thy feet, and fouledst their rivers. 3 Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will therefore spread out my net over thee with a company of many people; and they shall bring thee up in my net. 4 Then will I leave thee upon the land, I will cast thee forth upon the open field, and will cause all the fowls of the heaven to remain upon thee, and I will fill the beasts of the whole earth with thee. 5 And I will lay thy flesh upon the mountains, and fill the valleys with thy carcasses. 6 I will also water with thy blood the land wherein thou swimmest, even to the mountains; and the horizons shall be full of thee. 7 And when I shall put thee out, I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light. 8 All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee, and set darkness upon thy land, saith the Lord GOD. 9 I will also vex the hearts of many people, when I shall bring thy destruction among the nations, into the countries which thou hast not known. 10 Yea, I will make many people amazed at thee, and their kings shall be horribly afraid for thee, when I shall brandish my sword before them; and they shall tremble at every moment, every man for his own life, in the day of thy fall."

32.0.1.en: The last lamentation begins with Pharaoh, then his multitude, then the nations that imitated him or relied upon him. This lamentation came about two months after the news of the capture of Jerusalem reached the prophet Ezekiel and the men of the captivity.

32.1.0.en: The lamentation began thus: He said to him, "Thou art like a young lion (a lion) of the nations, and thou art as a crocodile in the seas" [2]. He imagined himself a lion protecting the nations from the king of Babylon, and did not realize that he was merely a crocodile confined to his river, unable to go out of the land of Egypt to rescue Jerusalem or any other city from the hands of Babylon. He thought himself able to deliver, and so he stirred up the king of Judah; and when Jerusalem was besieged he could not save her. He became like one who troubles the waters with his feet, so that he neither rests nor leaves others at rest. This is "the great crocodile that lieth in the midst of his rivers" (Ezek 29:3).

32.1.1.en: In chapter 29 the great crocodile boasted of himself, saying: "My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself" (Ezek 29:3, 9). This arrogant spirit did not destroy the crocodile alone, but destroyed the fish that clung to his scales as well. He flowed forth with the rivers of his pride over the rivers of others and fouled them with his feet [2]. Therefore his judgment became harsh and bitter, bringing death upon others also. For the Lord spread His net to catch this crocodile together with the fish, the many (peoples) who imitated him or clung to his scales (Ezek 32:3; 29:4).

32.2.s.en: The chastisements of the Lord are:

32.2.0.en: a. He repeats the same punishment mentioned in chapter 29. He brings him out of his river, the object of his boasting and arrogance, and casts him upon dry land to die with the fish that cling to him, and to become prey for the fowls of heaven and the beasts of the field.

32.3.0.en: b. Since this great crocodile prides himself on his Nile and the flood that it brings, which gives fertility to the land and enriches him with good things, therefore, instead of the flood of water, God floods the land with the blood of the crocodile until it reaches the mountains and the valleys are filled with it [6]. Pride turns the water into blood, and the blood of the proud man is poured out, bearing the smell of death which all loathe: the high mountains as well as the low valleys. Instead of words of boasting that draw many to take refuge in him, the smell of death rises, and all turn away from him.

32.4.0.en: c. When his blood goes out of him, this great crocodile becomes a stinking carcass cast upon the mountains and in the valleys. Having thought himself a support for others, he becomes a burden of stench which everyone wants to be rid of. He makes him and those around him "captives" in lands they do not know [9].

32.4.1.en: d. His judgment does not stop at his own destruction, the destruction of the peoples that clung to him, the turning of the river waters into deadly blood, and his becoming a burden from whose stinking carcass the mountains and valleys want to be rid. Rather, the effect of his pride reaches to the sun and the moon and the other stars, for it is said: "And when I shall put thee out, I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light. All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee, and set darkness upon thy land, saith the Lord GOD" [7-8].

32.4.2.en: This is a bitter picture of the signs of the end as the Lord Christ Himself proclaimed them (Mt 24:29), and of the signs of the false christ (Rev 8:12). It is as though the judgment of the proud man is a pledge of the great judgment, and a shadow of the age of the Antichrist!

32.4.3.en: What are these heavens whose light is covered, if not man's loss of every heavenly thought and his failure to taste eternal life? What are these stars that are darkened, if not the inner spiritual powers and the senses of the body? Instead of being the secret of inner enlightenment by the Holy Spirit, they become the secret of the soul's darkness and ruin. He covers the sun with a cloud, for the soul no longer sees its Christ, the Sun of Righteousness, shining within it; and the moon does not give her light, for the life of the Church, with its worship and its preaching, has no effect upon it. As for the land over which darkness is set, it is the body of man, which, instead of being a holy temple enlightened by the Lord, becomes a place of darkness.

32.4.4.en: In short, pride destroys man utterly. It deprives him of Christ, the Sun of Righteousness, and of the Church, the shining moon; it shatters his inner powers, corrupts his heart and his body, and darkens all his thoughts! Heaven and earth become dark for him, the sun and the moon as though they did not exist, and the stars fall within him.

32.5.0.en: e. In the face of this total ruin of soul and body, of mind and heart, a state of terror and trembling spreads among the many peoples with their kings, for it is said: "Yea, I will make many people amazed at thee, and their kings shall be horribly afraid for thee, when I shall brandish my sword before them; and they shall tremble at every moment, every man for his own life, in the day of thy fall" [10]. The destruction of the proud terrifies the hearts of sinners, for they feel that their own judgment has drawn near.

32.6.0.en: 11 "For thus saith the Lord GOD; The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee. 12 By the swords of the mighty will I cause thy multitude to fall, the terrible of the nations, all of them: and they shall spoil the pomp of Egypt, and all the multitude thereof shall be destroyed. 13 I will destroy also all the beasts thereof from beside the great waters; neither shall the foot of man trouble them any more, nor the hoofs of beasts trouble them. 14 Then will I make their waters deep, and cause their rivers to run like oil, saith the Lord GOD. 15 When I shall make the land of Egypt desolate, and the country shall be destitute of that whereof it was full, when I shall smite all them that dwell therein, then shall they know that I am the LORD. 16 This is the lamentation wherewith they shall lament her: the daughters of the nations shall lament her: they shall lament for her, even for Egypt, and for all her multitude, saith the Lord GOD."

32.6.1.en: The chastisement does not stop at Pharaoh, but reaches his multitude, who fall by the swords of the mighty men of the king of Babylon. The pride of Pharaoh, of his multitude and of his animals is shaken.

32.6.2.en: If Pharaoh represents the proud soul, then his multitude represents the powers of the soul, which work either for its building up or for its pulling down, while his animals signify the body with its senses and powers. Destruction embraces man with all his capacities, those of the soul and those of the body together.

32.6.3.en: As for the great waters that are dried up, they are God's gifts and free graces, which God withdraws from the arrogant soul.

32.7.s.en: 3. Lamentation over Pharaoh with the nations:

32.7.0.en: 17 It came to pass also in the twelfth year, in the fifteenth day of the month, that the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 18 "Son of man, wail for the multitude of Egypt, and cast them down, even her, and the daughters of the famous nations, unto the nether parts of the earth, with them that go down into the pit. 19 Whom dost thou pass in beauty? go down, and be thou laid with the uncircumcised. 20 They shall fall in the midst of them that are slain by the sword: she is delivered to the sword: draw her and all her multitudes. 21 The strong among the mighty shall speak to him out of the midst of hell with them that help him: they are gone down, they lie uncircumcised, slain by the sword. 22 Asshur is there and all her company: his graves are about him: all of them slain, fallen by the sword: 23 Whose graves are set in the sides of the pit, and her company is round about her grave: all of them slain, fallen by the sword, which caused terror in the land of the living. 24 There is Elam and all her multitude round about her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, which are gone down uncircumcised into the nether parts of the earth, which caused their terror in the land of the living; yet have they borne their shame with them that go down to the pit. 25 They have set her a bed in the midst of the slain with all her multitude: her graves are round about him: all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword: though their terror was caused in the land of the living, yet have they borne their shame with them that go down to the pit: he is put in the midst of them that be slain. 26 There is Meshech, Tubal, and all her multitude: her graves are round about him: all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword, though they caused their terror in the land of the living. 27 And they shall not lie with the mighty that are fallen of the uncircumcised, which are gone down to hell with their weapons of war: and they have laid their swords under their heads, but their iniquities shall be upon their bones, though they were the terror of the mighty in the land of the living. 28 Yea, thou shalt be broken in the midst of the uncircumcised, and shalt lie with them that are slain with the sword. 29 There is Edom, her kings, and all her princes, which with their might are laid by them that were slain by the sword: they shall lie with the uncircumcised, and with them that go down to the pit. 30 There be the princes of the north, all of them, and all the Zidonians, which are gone down with the slain; with their terror they are ashamed of their might; and they lie uncircumcised with them that be slain by the sword, and bear their shame with them that go down to the pit. 31 Pharaoh shall see them, and shall be comforted over all his multitude, even Pharaoh and all his army slain by the sword, saith the Lord GOD. 32 For I have caused my terror in the land of the living: and he shall be laid in the midst of the uncircumcised with them that are slain with the sword, even Pharaoh and all his multitude, saith the Lord GOD."

32.8.0.en: At the end of the prophecy against Pharaoh and his multitude, he joined with him in the lamentation "the daughters of the famous nations" [18], declaring that they should wail over them together with Pharaoh's multitude, because all of them have gone down to the nether parts of the earth with them that go down into the pit. Perhaps by those daughters he meant the nations that were bound to Pharaoh and his army and his authority, as women are bound to their men and seek their protection...

32.8.1.en: It is the end of the multitude of the nations to go down into the lower pit, into hell, as slain men cast down with the uncircumcised. This expression is repeated many times in this section [19, 25, 27, 29, 30, 31]. They were like mighty men who had terror and dread in the land of the living, and they went down with their uncleanness (the uncircumcised) as slain men cast down in hell.

32.9.0.en: Living examples were set before Pharaoh and his multitude of great nations that were like mighty men in the land of the living and ended up cast down like the uncircumcised, slain by the sword, going down to hell, such as Asshur [22], Elam [24], Meshech and Tubal [26], Edom [29] and all the Zidonians [30].

32.9.1.en: We have already spoken about these lands or kingdoms, except Elam, which is named after Elam son of Shem (Gen 10:22). In the days of Abraham, Chedorlaomer king of Elam was the leader of the kings of the East who invaded the Jordan region (Gen 14:1-11). The borders of this kingdom lay beyond the river Tigris, east of the kingdom of Babylon, south of Assyria and Media, north of the Persian Gulf, and west of Persia. Its capital was Shushan (Susa), and for that reason the Elamites were called Shushanchites. In the eighth century B.C. the kings of Assyria defeated Elam and took its men as mercenary soldiers in their army, and they took part in the attack on Jerusalem (Isa 22:6). The Medes (the Persians) annexed it to their empire and made it one of their provinces, and in consideration of its standing they made Shushan their capital (Dan 8:2). The Elamites were among the peoples who were carried to Samaria to dwell there after the captivity of Judah, and when the Jews returned from the captivity, the remnant of these immigrants were among those who opposed the idea of rebuilding the Temple (Ezra 4:9). Around 200 B.C. the Elamites regained their strength, and some of their kings gained power over cities in Babylon. Today Elam is part of Iran, called the province of Khuzestan.

32.9.2.en: Make me a lion's whelp, not a crocodile!

32.9.3.en: * Pharaoh put on the skin of a lion's whelp to protect the nations, and behold, he is a crocodile who devours the nations like the fish around him!

32.9.4.en: * With an arrogant spirit he claimed that he had made the Nile of Egypt with his own hands, and he did not know that by his pride he had fouled the waters of the Nile with his feet; he neither rested nor let the nations around him rest!

32.9.5.en: * Because of him the heavens covered their lights, and the earth was in darkness!

32.9.6.en: His soul (the heaven) was corrupted, and also his body (the earth)!

32.9.7.en: * Make me, O Lord, a lion's whelp, a son to You, O Lion that came out of the midst of Judah!

32.9.8.en: Grant me humility, that I may not trouble the water of grace in my heart!

32.9.9.en: Shine with Your light within me, O Sun of Righteousness, that my soul may shine like a new heaven!

32.9.10.en: And let my body be sanctified like a new earth!

33.0.0.en: 1 Again the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, speak to the children of thy people, and say unto them, When I bring the sword upon a land, if the people of the land take a man of their coasts, and set him for their watchman: 3 If when he seeth the sword come upon the land, he blow the trumpet, and warn the people; 4 Then whosoever heareth the sound of the trumpet, and taketh not warning; if the sword come, and take him away, his blood shall be upon his own head. 5 He heard the sound of the trumpet, and took not warning; his blood shall be upon him. But he that taketh warning shall deliver his soul. 6 But if the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet, and the people be not warned; if the sword come, and take any person from among them, he is taken away in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at the watchman's hand. 7 So thou, O son of man, I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; therefore thou shalt hear the word at my mouth, and warn them from me. 8 When I say unto the wicked, O wicked man, thou shalt surely die; if thou dost not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand. 9 Nevertheless, if thou warn the wicked of his way to turn from it; if he do not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul."

33.1.0.en: Before we speak of his responsibility, we would like to clarify that the Lord's address to him was thus: "Speak to the children of thy people" [2]. He did not say to him "the children of My people"; and likewise He says "as my people" [31], that is, as though they were My people. For since they had not yet enjoyed reconciliation with God, God does not call them "My people." This is what we saw in our study of the Book of Exodus: when God is in a state of reconciliation with His people, He says, "My people, My sabbaths, My feasts, My incense, My offerings..." attributing to Himself personally the people and all their worship, their feasts and their offerings. But in a state of grief on their account He says to the prophet "thy people," as He says to them "your feasts, your sabbaths, your offerings," and so on...

33.1.1.en: God had begun this group of prophecies and commandments with an indirect rebuke, saying to them: I can no longer call you My people... You are the people of Ezekiel, as though you were My people. Accept My commandment and enter into repentance, and I shall make you a people for Myself and I shall be a God to you; or as He said by the mouth of the prophet Ezekiel: "My dwelling place also shall be over them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people" (Ezek 37:27).

33.2.0.en: He then spoke of his responsibility as a watchman, bound to be frank for the salvation of their souls and the salvation of his own soul; for if he stops proclaiming the message out of courtesy to them, every soul that perishes will be required of him... "But if the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet, and the people be not warned; if the sword come, and take any person from among them, he is taken away in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at the watchman's hand" [6]. These words still terrify every bishop, priest or deacon... for if they neglect to warn the people, whatever their circumstances or positions, their own souls will be required in place of the souls that perish... We have already given examples of this.

33.2.1.en: The following are some comments of the Fathers on the responsibility of the watchmen and their obligation to warn sinners and not to be silent:

33.2.2.en: *According to what is written in Ezekiel, the watchmen must not keep silent about vice while the sword hangs over them, for this silence profits neither them nor the sinners; rather, they ought to watch and warn. In this those who give the warning are profited, though the two are not profited together, the speaker and the hearer.

33.2.3.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus *The first thing I do is to present to my people a report that I draw from above, that I may fulfil my work as a watchman (Isa 21:6; 62:6; Hab 2:1). If I do not stop the coming of the sword, I save my own soul and the souls of those who hear me, by proclaiming the disobedience of my people, counting what belongs to them as belonging to me. In this I obtain some rest and tenderness.

33.2.4.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus *The watchmen and overseers were set in the Church over the people in order to rebuke sin without mercy.

33.2.5.en: St. Augustine *What kind of blood does God require at the hand of the watchman, if not that which is poured out from the sinner? For thus the heart of the fool perishes, for it is said: "Hearken unto me, ye that have lost your hearts," since they poured out the blood and lost the strength of the living soul.

33.2.6.en: Origen *If you were entrusted with guarding a spring of pure water for the flock, and saw the flock drinking mud, would you not work to remove the mud from the water? But now you are not tending a spring of water but of blood and spirit. If you see one in whom there is sin, which is more dangerous than dust and mud, and he comes to it, will you not grieve? Will you not prevent him? What excuse have you? For God has given you this honor for this purpose, that you may distinguish these things. This is your office; here is your peace, and here is your crown, not merely that you wear a shining white garment!

33.3.s.en: 2. We do not despair, for God is merciful:

33.3.0.en: 10 "Therefore, O thou son of man, speak unto the house of Israel; Thus ye speak, saying, If our transgressions and our sins be upon us, and we pine away in them, how should we then live? 11 Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?"

33.3.1.en: If the prophet was bound to be perfectly frank in proclaiming the divine commandment and the prophecies, without flattery or courtesy, for the salvation of their souls and of his own soul as well, this does not mean that he should be harsh with them. If he had spoken violently before, it was because the danger of the captivity was coming; but now that the captivity has actually taken place and all have come under the bitterness of the bitter cup, there is no need for despair; rather, the proclamation of God's mercies and His love for mankind begins, even in the midst of His harsh chastisements.

33.3.3.en: If our transgressions and our sins be upon us, and we pine away in them, how should we then live?

33.3.5.en: As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live:

33.3.6.en: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?" [10-11].

33.3.7.en: Formerly they drank iniquity like water, making light of sin and its power in their lives; and when they began to fall under chastisement in earnest, they were assailed by despair, saying that they were pining away, that is, perishing, so how could they live after that...? But the Lord, who rebuked them bitterly before the chastisement, now soothes them with love, lest they be crushed by the cutting off of hope.

33.3.8.en: The Fathers comment on these divine words that give hope as follows:

33.3.9.en: *Through these divine words the sinner returns to hope, but there is also another snare which he fears, namely that through this very hope he sins all the more (making light of sin).

33.3.10.en: St. Augustine *Let him love, because God desires mercy rather than sacrifice (Hos 6:6), and let him fear, because He hates sin!

33.3.11.en: Let him love, for God desires the repentance of the sinner and not his death, and let him fear, for He hates the sinners who do not repent!

33.3.12.en: Tertullian *It is the mission of the Savior to call sinners, not the righteous, for, as He Himself said: "They that be whole need not a physician" (Mt 9:12-13).

33.3.13.en: He desires the repentance of the sinner and not his death (Ezek 33:11), and He carries on His shoulders the poor lost sheep. And thus when the prodigal son returned, his father received him with joy.

33.4.s.en: 3. God does not reckon with us for our past:

33.4.0.en: 12 "Therefore, thou son of man, say unto the children of thy people, The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression: as for the wickedness of the wicked, he shall not fall thereby in the day that he turneth from his wickedness; neither shall the righteous be able to live for his righteousness in the day that he sinneth. 13 When I shall say to the righteous, that he shall surely live; if he trust to his own righteousness, and commit iniquity, all his righteousnesses shall not be remembered; but for his iniquity that he hath committed, he shall die for it. 14 Again, when I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; if he turn from his sin, and do that which is lawful and right; 15 If the wicked restore the pledge, give again that he had robbed, walk in the statutes of life, without committing iniquity; he shall surely live, he shall not die. 16 None of his sins that he hath committed shall be mentioned unto him: he hath done that which is lawful and right; he shall surely live. 17 Yet the children of thy people say, The way of the Lord is not equal: but as for them, their way is not equal. 18 When the righteous turneth from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, he shall even die thereby. 19 But if the wicked turn from his wickedness, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall live thereby. 20 Yet ye say, The way of the Lord is not equal. O ye house of Israel, I will judge you every one after his ways."

33.4.1.en: When the Lord opens to us the door of hope, He wants us to enter it with all strength and without fear, and so He offers us every assurance. He does not reckon with us for our past, nor even for our present, if we now offer sincere repentance. He does not desire our destruction, but seeks our salvation by every way, offering us every possibility of returning to Him. At the same time, since God fears for His children who stand lest they fall, He warns them not to rely on their past, lest they become careless and fall...

33.4.2.en: St. Jerome says: [In the life of Christians we look not at the beginnings but at the ends. Paul began in a bad way, but his end was good. The beginning of Judas was worthy of praise, but his end was blameworthy because of his betrayal...

33.4.3.en: The life of the Christian is the true ladder of Jacob, upon which the angels ascend and descend, while the Lord stands upon it, stretching out His hands to those who slip, supporting them, and looking upon those who ascend the painful steps].

33.4.4.en: We saw in our interpretation of chapter eighteen how Origen used it to answer those who speak of a difference of human natures, showing that the wicked can repent and the righteous can fall... For some thought that man has a good or an evil nature that cannot be changed. Among his words: [The soul of the righteous man is subject to change, as Ezekiel testifies, saying that the righteous man can forsake the commandments of God, and his former righteousness is not reckoned to him].

33.4.5.en: If the righteous man turns back from his righteous life in the Lord he dies, while if the wicked man repents of his wickedness he finds the life in Christ taking him up.

33.4.6.en: "When the righteous turneth from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, he shall even die thereby.

33.5.0.en: But if the wicked turn from his wickedness, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall live thereby" [18-19].

33.6.0.en: Let us therefore beware of sin lest we die; and if we have died by it, let us receive the Lord our righteousness and live by Him. St. Ambrose says: [Everyone who gives himself up to evil pleasures is dead, for "she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth" (1 Tim 5:6), and those who are without faith go down to hell while they are still alive, even if they seem to be alive with us, for they are in hell. Everyone who takes usury or commits theft is not living, as you read in Ezekiel. But if that man keeps the commandments of the Lord to do them, he lives, and he lives by them [19]... Let us then hasten to that life, for whoever touches Life lives. And the woman truly touched it, she who touched the hem of His garment and was healed, and was freed from death, and it was said to her: "Thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace" (Lk 8:48; Mt 9:22). If he that touches a dead body is unclean, then he who touched the Living One is truly saved. Let us then seek this Living One, but take care not to seek Him among the dead, lest it be said to us as to the women: "Why seek ye the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen" (Lk 24:5-6).

33.7.0.en: 21 And it came to pass in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month, in the fifth day of the month, that one that had escaped out of Jerusalem came unto me, saying, "The city is smitten." 22 Now the hand of the LORD was upon me in the evening, afore he that was escaped came; and had opened my mouth, until he came to me in the morning; and my mouth was opened, and I was no more dumb. 23 Then the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 24 "Son of man, they that inhabit those wastes of the land of Israel speak, saying, Abraham was one, and he inherited the land: but we are many; the land is given us for inheritance. 25 Wherefore say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Ye eat with the blood, and lift up your eyes toward your idols, and shed blood: and shall ye possess the land? 26 Ye stand upon your sword, ye work abomination, and ye defile every one his neighbour's wife: and shall ye possess the land? 27 Say thou thus unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; As I live, surely they that are in the wastes shall fall by the sword, and him that is in the open field will I give to the beasts to be devoured, and they that be in the forts and in the caves shall die of the pestilence. 28 For I will lay the land most desolate, and the pomp of her strength shall cease; and the mountains of Israel shall be desolate, that none shall pass through. 29 Then shall they know that I am the LORD, when I have laid the land most desolate because of all their abominations which they have committed."

33.8.0.en: A man from Jerusalem was able to escape when the city was smitten and to run to where the prophet Ezekiel and the captive people were, to tell them of the smiting of Jerusalem. This was in the twelfth year of the first captivity of Judah, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month; that is, the news reached them after about six months. Here his mouth was opened to speak and Ezekiel was no longer silent [22], since all heard the truth of his prophecies which he had declared to them before.

33.9.0.en: They had said to him before that if God gave all this land as an inheritance to Abraham, who was one man, would He not give them this land, they being many? [24] How far are God's measures from man's! God looks upon the heart and gives generously to the pure heart, even if it is unique in the world, and does not give on account of multitude. Man, however, looks not to purity of heart but to abundance of number. They thought that God would never forsake the city or the Temple, whatever abominations they committed, so long as they offered Him sacrifices and offerings, even if their hearts were devoted to idols and turned aside to evil. God desires pure worship, not an abundance of ordinances and formalism in worship! Abraham, the obedient believer, was worthy to inherit all this land, while among those myriads of his descendants at that time there was found none worthy of the inheritance!!! How much the Church needs true saints in whose hearts God may rest, even if their numbers are very few! Therefore the word of God came to the prophet Ezekiel that they should be purified and so inherit the land. In other words, that they should become like Abraham their father and so be worthy to inherit him!

33.9.1.en: This is repentance... It is a return to the holy, hidden life!

33.10.s.en: 5. A return of the heart, not of form:

33.10.0.en: 30 "Also, thou son of man, the children of thy people still are talking against thee by the walls and in the doors of the houses, and speak one to another, every one to his brother, saying, Come, I pray you, and hear what is the word that cometh forth from the LORD. 31 And they come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness. 32 And, lo, thou art unto them as a very lovely song of one that hath a pleasant voice, and can play well on an instrument: for they hear thy words, but they do them not. 33 And when this cometh to pass, (lo, it will come,) then shall they know that a prophet hath been among them."

33.10.1.en: When the news arrived, crowds flocked to Ezekiel to listen to him. They had come to know that he spoke only the truth. Perhaps they also flocked to him in great numbers and with longing because, after he had been speaking to them words of rebuke and repentance before the fall of Jerusalem, he began to speak of vengeance on the wicked who rejoiced at their fall (Ezek 25-32) and to give hope of return and restoration. Perhaps, too, they came to him to listen to his wonderful literary style.

33.11.0.en: The prophet feared that they would come to him to listen merely for intellectual pleasure or passing delight, and not for sincere repentance, for the Lord said to him: "They come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness" [31]. His words became like measured poetry presented in a beautiful voice to the tunes of music, which they enjoy for a while and do not do! God does not want mere enjoyment; He wants action... sincere repentance that comes from the heart, and that is practical!

33.11.1.en: Take away from me the spirit of failure!

33.11.2.en: * How wonderful You are, O Lord, in Your plan toward us!

33.11.3.en: You permitted harsh chastisement for the people, even to the Babylonian captivity, and You threatened to destroy the holy city Jerusalem and its Temple, and You asked Your prophet, as a watchman, to speak the truth even if it wounds!

33.11.4.en: And yet, in spite of all this, when the people were taken captive, You take despair away from them!

33.11.5.en: You urge them to sincere repentance filled with hope!

33.11.6.en: * Behold, I am in Your hands, O Savior of my soul!

33.11.7.en: Who can rescue me from the feeling of failure but You!

33.11.8.en: In Your chastisement of me, hold my depths that they may not collapse!

33.11.9.en: Reveal Yourself within me, that my soul may not be shattered!

33.11.10.en: Make me repent, and support me with the spirit of hope!

33.11.11.en: *You, my Lord, care for the heart and not the form!

33.11.12.en: You seek one holy heart like the heart of Abraham, better than many who mix truth with falsehood!

33.11.13.en: Sanctify us! Count us the few holy ones for Yourself!

33.11.14.en: Take over my heart, my mind and my feelings!

33.11.15.en: Take over my body and my conduct!

33.11.16.en: I am in Your hands; I ask for the work of Your Holy Spirit in me!
